### **Clinical Trial**

Load the Gait data

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
load("data/gait.Rda")
```

1.  Plot each participants' gait data and describe it using descriptive statistics. Which of these descriptive statistics do you think is most useful for capturing the overall gait smoothness and balance of a participant?

    *Thoughts:*

    To plot each participants data, I first want to look at how the the data varies across the 700s. Therefore, I will create a histogram showing the counts for each angle observed across the timeframe

Check for Missing Values:

```{r}
sum(is.na(gait_data))
```

No missing values, therefore continue with analysis. (Still need to check for outliers)

```{r}
#Obtain max and Min values
seconds <- gait_data[grepl("_secs$", names(gait_data))]

min(as.matrix(seconds), na.rm = TRUE)
max(as.matrix(seconds), na.rm = TRUE)
```

```{r}
measurement_cols <- grepl("_secs$", names(gait_data))
participants <- unique(na.omit(gait_data$donorid))

# Collect measurements for each participant
participant_values <- lapply(participants, function(id) {
  values <- as.numeric(unlist(
    gait_data[gait_data$donorid %in% id, measurement_cols]
  ))
  values[is.finite(values)]
})

# Calculate histograms and a shared y-axis limit
histograms <- lapply(participant_values, function(values) {
  hist(values, breaks = shared_breaks, plot = FALSE)
})

max_count <- max(vapply(histograms, function(h) max(h$counts), numeric(1)))

# Draw all histograms in a grid (4 × 4 for 16 participants)
local({
  old_par <- par(no.readonly = TRUE)
  on.exit(par(old_par))
  
  n_cols <- ceiling(sqrt(length(participants)))
  n_rows <- ceiling(length(participants) / n_cols)
  
  par(
    mfrow = c(n_rows, n_cols),
    mar = c(3, 3, 2, 1),
    mgp = c(1.8, 0.5, 0)
  )
  
  for (i in seq_along(participants)) {
    plot(
      histograms[[i]],
      freq = TRUE,
      xlim = c(-52, 62),
      ylim = c(0, max_count),
      xaxs = "i",
      xaxt = "n",
      main = as.character(participants[i]),
      xlab = "Measurement value",
      ylab = "Frequency",
      col = "steelblue",
      border = "white"
    )
    
    axis(1, at = seq(-50, 60, by = 10), cex.axis = 0.65)
  }
})
```

Now I am going to try make a graph that represents the variation of angle for each participant over their 700s

```{r}
# Find measurement columns and put them in time order
measurement_cols <- grep(
  "^[0-9]+_secs$", names(gait_data), value = TRUE
)

seconds <- as.numeric(sub("_secs$", "", measurement_cols))
time_order <- order(seconds)

measurement_cols <- measurement_cols[time_order]
seconds <- seconds[time_order]

# Colours represent time: blue -> yellow -> red
time_palette <- colorRampPalette(
  c("blue", "gold", "red")
)(700)

time_colours <- time_palette[seconds]

local({
  old_par <- par(no.readonly = TRUE)
  on.exit(par(old_par))
  
  n <- nrow(gait_data)
  n_cols <- ceiling(sqrt(n))
  n_rows <- ceiling(n / n_cols)
  
  par(
    mfrow = c(n_rows, n_cols),
    mar = c(1, 1, 2, 1),
    oma = c(3, 0, 2, 0)
  )
  
  for (i in seq_len(n)) {
    angles <- as.numeric(unlist(
      gait_data[i, measurement_cols, drop = FALSE]
    ))
    
    # Convert degrees to radians
    radians <- angles * pi / 180
    valid <- is.finite(radians)
    
    # Empty panel, with equal horizontal and vertical scales
    plot(
      NA,
      xlim = c(-1.2, 1.2),
      ylim = c(-0.15, 1.2),
      asp = 1,
      axes = FALSE,
      xlab = "",
      ylab = "",
      main = as.character(gait_data$donorid[i])
    )
    
    # Semicircular guide
    arc <- seq(-pi / 2, pi / 2, length.out = 200)
    lines(sin(arc), cos(arc), col = "grey75")
    
    # Angle guides and labels
    ticks <- seq(-90, 90, by = 45)
    tick_radians <- ticks * pi / 180
    
    segments(
      0, 0,
      sin(tick_radians), cos(tick_radians),
      col = "grey80", lty = 2
    )
    
    text(
      1.12 * sin(tick_radians),
      1.12 * cos(tick_radians),
      labels = paste0(ticks, "°"),
      cex = 0.7
    )
    
    # One ray for each recorded time point
    segments(
      0, 0,
      sin(radians[valid]),
      cos(radians[valid]),
      col = adjustcolor(time_colours[valid], alpha.f = 0.3),
      lwd = 0.7
    )
    
    points(0, 0, pch = 16, cex = 0.6)
  }
  
  mtext("Walking orientation by participant",
        outer = TRUE, side = 3, line = 0.5)
  
  mtext("Time: blue = 1 s   |   yellow ≈ 350 s   |   red = 700 s",
        outer = TRUE, side = 1, line = 1)
})
```

```{r}
# Find measurement columns and put them in time order
measurement_cols <- grep(
  "^[0-9]+_secs$", names(gait_data), value = TRUE
)

seconds <- as.numeric(sub("_secs$", "", measurement_cols))
measurement_cols <- measurement_cols[order(seconds)]

if (length(measurement_cols) == 0 || nrow(gait_data) == 0) {
  stop("No participant rows or seconds columns found.")
}

# Shared colour scale for all participants
angle_palette <- colorRampPalette(c("blue", "red"))(256)
red_threshold <- 20

local({
  old_par <- par(no.readonly = TRUE)
  on.exit(par(old_par))
  
  # Arrange participants in a grid
  n <- nrow(gait_data)
  n_cols <- ceiling(sqrt(n))
  n_rows <- ceiling(n / n_cols)
  
  par(
    mfrow = c(n_rows, n_cols),
    mar = c(1, 1, 2, 1),
    oma = c(3, 0, 2, 0)
  )
  
  for (i in seq_len(n)) {
    angles <- as.numeric(unlist(
      gait_data[i, measurement_cols, drop = FALSE]
    ))
    
    # Convert degrees to radians
    radians <- angles * pi / 180
    valid <- is.finite(radians)
    
    # Blue at 0°, fully red at ±15° and beyond
    colour_index <- 1L + floor(
      pmin(abs(angles[valid]) / red_threshold, 1) * 255
    )
    
    angle_colours <- angle_palette[colour_index]
    
    # Create an empty panel
    plot(
      NA,
      xlim = c(-1.2, 1.2),
      ylim = c(-0.15, 1.2),
      asp = 1,
      axes = FALSE,
      xlab = "",
      ylab = "",
      main = as.character(gait_data$donorid[i])
    )
    
    # Semicircular guide
    arc <- seq(-pi / 2, pi / 2, length.out = 200)
    lines(sin(arc), cos(arc), col = "grey75")
    
    # Angle guides and labels
    ticks <- seq(-90, 90, by = 45)
    tick_radians <- ticks * pi / 180
    
    segments(
      0, 0,
      sin(tick_radians), cos(tick_radians),
      col = "grey80",
      lty = 2
    )
    
    text(
      1.12 * sin(tick_radians),
      1.12 * cos(tick_radians),
      labels = paste0(ticks, "°"),
      cex = 0.7
    )
    
    # One ray for each valid measurement
    segments(
      0, 0,
      sin(radians[valid]),
      cos(radians[valid]),
      col = adjustcolor(angle_colours, alpha.f = 0.5),
      lwd = 0.7
    )
    
    points(0, 0, pch = 16, cex = 0.6)
  }
  
  mtext(
    "Walking orientation by participant",
    outer = TRUE, side = 3, line = 0.5
  )
  
  mtext(
    sprintf(
      "Distance from vertical: blue = 0° | red = %.0f° and above",
      red_threshold
    ),
    outer = TRUE, side = 1, line = 1
  )
})
```

Trying to organise by groups:

```{r}
# Change participants ID numbers to 1-16
gait_data$participant_label <- paste("Participant", seq_len(nrow(gait_data)))

# Find measurement columns and put them in time order
measurement_cols <- grep(
  "^[0-9]+_secs$", names(gait_data), value = TRUE
)

seconds <- as.numeric(sub("_secs$", "", measurement_cols))
measurement_cols <- measurement_cols[order(seconds)]

if (length(measurement_cols) == 0 || nrow(gait_data) == 0) {
  stop("No participant rows or seconds columns found.")
}

# Define the four groups using the labels in your dataset
treatment <- trimws(as.character(gait_data$treatment))
exercise <- tolower(trimws(as.character(gait_data$exercise)))

groups <- list(
  "Control\nNo Exercise" = which(
    treatment == "L-DOPA control" & exercise == "n"
  ),
  "Control\nExercise" = which(
    treatment == "L-DOPA control" & exercise == "y"
  ),
  "New Drug\nNo Exercise" = which(
    treatment == "New compound" & exercise == "n"
  ),
  "New Drug\nExercise" = which(
    treatment == "New compound" & exercise == "y"
  )
)

# Sort participants within each group by donor ID
groups <- lapply(groups, function(rows) {
  rows[order(gait_data$donorid[rows])]
})

# Check that everyone has been assigned to a group
if (sum(lengths(groups)) != nrow(gait_data)) {
  stop("Some treatment or exercise labels do not match the four groups.")
}

# Shared colour scale: blue at 0°, red at ±15° and beyond
angle_palette <- colorRampPalette(c("blue", "red"))(256)
red_threshold <- 20

local({
  old_par <- par(no.readonly = TRUE)
  on.exit(par(old_par))
  
  n_rows <- max(lengths(groups))
  n_cols <- length(groups)
  
  par(
    mfrow = c(n_rows, n_cols),
    mar = c(2.5, 1, 2, 1),
    oma = c(3, 0, 5, 0)
  )
  
  # Fill the grid row by row, keeping each group in its own column
  for (row in seq_len(n_rows)) {
    for (group in seq_along(groups)) {
      
      # Leave a blank panel if this group has fewer participants
      if (row > length(groups[[group]])) {
        plot.new()
        next
      }
      
      i <- groups[[group]][row]
      
      angles <- as.numeric(unlist(
        gait_data[i, measurement_cols, drop = FALSE]
      ))
      
      radians <- angles * pi / 180
      valid <- is.finite(radians)
      
      colour_index <- 1L + floor(
        pmin(abs(angles[valid]) / red_threshold, 1) * 255
      )
      
      angle_colours <- angle_palette[colour_index]
      
      # Create participant panel
      plot(
        NA,
        xlim = c(-1.1, 1.1),
        ylim = c(-0.01, 1.1),
        asp = 1,
        axes = FALSE,
        xlab = "",
        ylab = ""
      )
      
      # Semicircular guide
      arc <- seq(-pi / 2, pi / 2, length.out = 200)
      lines(sin(arc), cos(arc), col = "grey75")
      
      # Angle guides and labels
      ticks <- seq(-90, 90, by = 45)
      tick_radians <- ticks * pi / 180
      
      segments(
        0, 0,
        sin(tick_radians), cos(tick_radians),
        col = "grey80",
        lty = 2
      )
      
      text(
        1.12 * sin(tick_radians),
        1.12 * cos(tick_radians),
        labels = paste0(ticks, "°"),
        cex = 1
      )
      
      # Draw one ray per valid measurement
      segments(
        0, 0,
        sin(radians[valid]),
        cos(radians[valid]),
        col = adjustcolor(angle_colours, alpha.f = 0.5),
        lwd = 0.7
      )
      
      points(0, 0, pch = 16, cex = 0.6)
      mtext(
        gait_data$participant_label[i],
        side = 1,
        line = 0.5,
        cex = 0.8,
        font = 2
      )
    }
  }
  
  # Column headings
  for (group in seq_along(groups)) {
    mtext(
      names(groups)[group],
      outer = TRUE,
      side = 3,
      at = (group - 0.5) / n_cols,
      line = -1,
      font = 2,
      cex = 1.1
    )
  }
  
  mtext(
    "Walking orientation by participant",
    outer = TRUE, side = 3, line = 3.5,
    font = 2,
    cex = 1.4
  )
  
  mtext(
    "Distance from vertical: blue = 0° | red = 20° and above",
    outer = TRUE, side = 1, line = 1
  )
})
```

Running Descriptive Statistics on Gait Data:

Getting Interquartile range, max, min, mean (Boxplots).

Grouped by Treatment Group, ordered by IQR size

```{r}
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

# Convert the time columns into one measurement column
gait_long <- gait_data |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = matches("^[0-9]+_secs$"),
    names_to = "time",
    values_to = "gait_value"
  )

# Order participants by ascending IQR
participant_order <- gait_long |>
  group_by(treatment, participant_label) |>
  summarise(iqr = IQR(gait_value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  arrange(treatment, iqr) |>
  pull(participant_label)

gait_long <- gait_long |>
  mutate(
    participant_label = factor(
      participant_label,
      levels = unique(participant_order)
    )
  )

# Create one boxplot per participant
ggplot(gait_long, aes(
  x = participant_label,
  y = gait_value,
  fill = treatment
)) +
  geom_boxplot(
    outlier.colour = "red",
    na.rm = TRUE
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(-60, 60, by = 15)) +
  coord_flip(ylim = c(-60, 60)) +
  facet_grid(
    rows = vars(treatment),
    scales = "free_y",
    space = "free_y"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of gait measurements by participant",
    x = "Participant",
    y = "Gait measurement"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```


Now making groups by age bracket (turning binary) and producing boxplots:

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

# Calculate the median age across participants
median_age <- gait_long |>
  distinct(participant_label, age) |>
  summarise(cutoff = median(age, na.rm = TRUE)) |>
  pull(cutoff)

median_age  # View the cutoff

# Create two age groups
gait_long <- gait_long |>
  mutate(
    age_group = case_when(
      age < median_age  ~ "Younger",
      age >= median_age ~ "Older"
    )
  )

# One boxplot per age group
ggplot(
  filter(gait_long, !is.na(age_group)),
  aes(x = age_group, y = gait_value, fill = age_group)
) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.colour = "red", na.rm = TRUE) +
  scale_x_discrete(limits = c("Younger", "Older")) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(-60, 60, by = 15)) +
  coord_flip(ylim = c(-60, 60)) +
  labs(
    title = "Gait measurements by age group",
    subtitle = paste0(
      "Median age: ", round(median_age, 2),
      " years; younger < median, older ≥ median"
    ),
    x = NULL,
    y = "Gait measurement"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

Separate into the four experimental groups:

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

# Define the four groups
gait_long <- gait_long |>
  mutate(
    group = case_when(
      grepl("control", treatment, ignore.case = TRUE) & exercise == "n" ~
        "control + no exercise",
      grepl("control", treatment, ignore.case = TRUE) & exercise == "y" ~
        "control + exercise",
      treatment == "New compound" & exercise == "n" ~
        "treatment + no exercise",
      treatment == "New compound" & exercise == "y" ~
        "treatment + exercise"
    ),
    group = factor(
      group,
      levels = c(
        "control + no exercise",
        "control + exercise",
        "treatment + no exercise",
        "treatment + exercise"
      )
    )
  )

# Order participants by IQR within each group
participant_order <- gait_long |>
  group_by(group, participant_label) |>
  summarise(iqr = IQR(gait_value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  arrange(group, iqr) |>
  pull(participant_label) |>
  as.character()

gait_long <- gait_long |>
  mutate(
    participant_label = factor(
      participant_label,
      levels = unique(participant_order)
    )
  )

# Plot the four groups
ggplot(gait_long, aes(
  x = participant_label,
  y = gait_value,
  fill = group
)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.colour = "red", na.rm = TRUE) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(-60, 60, by = 15)) +
  coord_flip(ylim = c(-60, 60)) +
  facet_grid(
    rows = vars(group),
    scales = "free_y",
    space = "free_y"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Gait measurements by treatment and exercise",
    x = "Participant",
    y = "Gait measurement"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

```{r}
participant_order <- gait_long |>
  group_by(group, participant_label) |>
  summarise(iqr = IQR(gait_value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  arrange(group, iqr) |>
  pull(participant_label) |>
  as.character()

gait_long <- gait_long |>
  mutate(
    participant_label = factor(
      participant_label,
      levels = unique(participant_order)
    )
  )

# Create age labels after setting the participant order
age_labels <- gait_long |>
  distinct(group, participant_label, age)

# Create age labels after setting the participant order
age_labels <- gait_long |>
  distinct(group, participant_label, age)

# Plot the four groups with age labels
ggplot(gait_long, aes(
  x = participant_label,
  y = gait_value,
  fill = group
)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.colour = "red", na.rm = TRUE) +
  geom_label(
    data = age_labels,
    aes(
      x = participant_label,
      y = 58,
      label = paste0("Age ", round(age, 1))
    ),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    hjust = 1,
    size = 3,
    fill = "white",
    colour = "black",
    linewidth = 0
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(-60, 60, by = 15)) +
  coord_flip(ylim = c(-60, 60)) +
  facet_grid(
    rows = vars(group),
    scales = "free_y",
    space = "free_y"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Gait measurements ordered by IQR within each group",
    x = "Participant",
    y = "Gait measurement"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

Now with average Age per group:

```{r}
# Define the four groups
gait_long <- gait_long |>
  mutate(
    group = case_when(
      grepl("control", treatment, ignore.case = TRUE) & exercise == "n" ~
        "control + no exercise",
      grepl("control", treatment, ignore.case = TRUE) & exercise == "y" ~
        "control + exercise",
      treatment == "New compound" & exercise == "n" ~
        "treatment + no exercise",
      treatment == "New compound" & exercise == "y" ~
        "treatment + exercise"
    ),
    group = factor(
      group,
      levels = c(
        "control + no exercise",
        "control + exercise",
        "treatment + no exercise",
        "treatment + exercise"
      )
    )
  )

# Order participants by IQR within each group
participant_order <- gait_long |>
  group_by(group, participant_label) |>
  summarise(iqr = IQR(gait_value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  arrange(group, iqr) |>
  pull(participant_label) |>
  as.character()

gait_long <- gait_long |>
  mutate(
    participant_label = factor(
      participant_label,
      levels = unique(participant_order)
    )
  )

# Create age labels after setting the participant order
age_labels <- gait_long |>
  distinct(group, participant_label, age)

# Create age labels after setting the participant order
age_labels <- gait_long |>
  distinct(group, participant_label, age)

# Calculate average age per group, counting each participant once
group_ages <- gait_long |>
  distinct(group, participant_label, age) |>
  group_by(group) |>
  summarise(
    mean_age = mean(age, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Plot the four groups with age labels
ggplot(gait_long, aes(
  x = participant_label,
  y = gait_value,
  fill = group
)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.colour = "red", na.rm = TRUE) +
  geom_label(
    data = group_ages,
    aes(
      x = Inf,
      y = 58,
      label = paste0("Mean age: ", round(mean_age, 1))
    ),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    hjust = 1,
    vjust = 1,
    size = 3,
    fill = "white",
    colour = "black",
    linewidth = 0
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(-60, 60, by = 15)) +
  coord_flip(ylim = c(-60, 60)) +
  facet_grid(
    rows = vars(group),
    scales = "free_y",
    space = "free_y"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Gait measurements ordered by IQR within each group",
    x = "Participant",
    y = "Gait measurement"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

Assumptions to Check:

If I want to run a linear or mixed linear model;

- A normal linear regression assumes independence of outcome data. This is not true, as the 700 observations are in a time series to each participant.

```{r}

```

Other tests worth analysing:

```{r}
library(dplyr)

# One row per participant
participant_stats <- gait_long |>
  group_by(donorid, treatment, exercise, age) |>
  summarise(
    n_observations = sum(!is.na(gait_value)),
    mean_gait = mean(gait_value, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_gait = median(gait_value, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_gait = sd(gait_value, na.rm = TRUE),
    iqr_gait = IQR(gait_value, na.rm = TRUE),
    rms_gait = sqrt(mean(gait_value^2, na.rm = TRUE)),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    treatment = factor(treatment),
    exercise = factor(exercise, levels = c("n", "y"))
  )

participant_stats
```

Using Root Square Mean to compare deviations from upright:

```{r}
model_treatment <- lm(
  rms_gait ~ treatment,
  data = participant_stats
)

summary(model_treatment)
confint(model_treatment)
```

Using Standard Deviation:

```{r}
model_treatment <- lm(
  sd_gait ~ treatment,
  data = participant_stats
)

summary(model_treatment)
confint(model_treatment)
```

Checking the reference group:

```{r}
levels(participant_stats$treatment)
```

Accounting for exercise and age, Using RMS:

```{r}
model_adjusted <- lm(
  rms_gait ~ treatment + exercise + age,
  data = participant_stats
)

summary(model_adjusted)
confint(model_adjusted)

# Test each predictor while accounting for the other two
drop1(model_adjusted, test = "F")
```

Accounting for Exercise and Age, using SD:

```{r}
model_adjusted <- lm(
  sd_gait ~ treatment + exercise + age,
  data = participant_stats
)

summary(model_adjusted)
confint(model_adjusted)

# Test each predictor while accounting for the other two
drop1(model_adjusted, test = "F")
```

Running graph for Root Square Means:

```{r}
ggplot(
  participant_stats,
  aes(x = treatment, y = rms_gait)
) +
  geom_boxplot(
    width = 0.5,
    fill = "grey90",
    outlier.shape = NA
  ) +
  geom_point(
    aes(colour = exercise, size = age),
    position = position_jitter(width = 0.08, height = 0, seed = 345),
    alpha = 0.7
  ) +
  scale_colour_manual(
    values = c("n" = "#D55E00", "y" = "#0072B2"),
    labels = c("n" = "No exercise", "y" = "Exercise"),
    name = "Exercise"
  ) +
  scale_size_continuous(
    name = "Age (years)",
    range = c(1, 6),
    guide = guide_legend(reverse = TRUE)
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(0, NA),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.1))
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Gait deviation from upright by treatment",
    x = "Treatment",
    y = "Participant RMS (degrees)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
